newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia says will stick to EU goal after poll.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia says will stick to EU goal after poll.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Friday he expected next month's general elections not to change the country's commitment to join the European Union (EU) as soon as possible.

"As head of the largest parliamentary party I can say that it is my goal to shape a strong pro-European coalition which will continue on the current path," Drnovsek said at an open meeting with a European Parliament delegation.

Slovenia holds its third multi-party general elections on November 10. Drnovsek's Liberal Democrats hold 30 of the parliament's 90 seats. Their junior coalition partner, the Christian Democrats, have 15.

Drnovsek said he expected Slovenia's parliament soon to ratify an association agreement with the EU, concluded in June, so that negotiations for full membership could get under way. The accord must be ratified by Slovenia and all EU member countries individually before it can be enforced.
European Parliament representatives said they expected the EU assembly to ratify the association agreement on October 23.

"There are a number of political parties in Slovenia that have some reservations concerning the ratification. We do not want Slovenia to be late in ratifying the agreement as that would endanger its pole position among candidates for full EU membership," said Michl Ebner, head of the EU delegation.

The right-wing People's Party, which has 12 seats in parliament, and a number of smaller groups have expressed strong reservations about Slovenia's drive to join the EU. They are unhappy about required amendments to the country's strict property ownership laws that would enable foreigners to buy real estate in Slovenia.
Drnovsek said delays were not likely, however, as Slovenia's parliament had already agreed to liberalise its property laws in April and parliament would stick to the decision.
